submission.justification: T1 has the best unirradiated resolution (about 6 um) but only 82% efficiency at 2e16, which fails the hard 97% requirement. T2 and T3 both pass. T2 resolves better than T3 (about 9 vs 14.7 um). The T2 thickness scan is shallow and flat from about 125 to 175 um (8.98, 9.08 and 8.94 um). The differences there are probably within noise. I chose 150 um, the middle of that range. The irradiation results are per technology, and the documents don't say what thickness was irradiated. So I could not confirm that efficiency holds at 150 um.

requirements.evidence: T2 measured 98.5% in the 2026 test beam. The irradiated sensor's thickness is not stated, so this is not confirmed for 150 um specifically.

requirements.requirement: Technology is one of the three candidates

requirements.evidence: T2 at 150 um gives 9.08 um in simulation. It is the best of the technologies that pass the efficiency requirement, and the 125-175 um scan values are within noise of each other. T1 is better (6 um) but fails efficiency.
